Criteria.TestCondition: The user can pause, stop, hide, or control the frequency of automatically updating content.
DisabilityImpact: With Limited Language, Cognitive, and Learning Abilities
Criteria.TesterComment: This test could not be performed: We watched this page for 6.5 seconds without touching it, looking for content that is still changing by itself after 5 seconds, like a carousel, ticker or counter. Nothing was, but we saw signs that the page may update by itself: it sets a timer of 86400 s, longer than we watched; the carousel "The systems powering the Science Discovery Engine were recen" changed until 0.5 s and then stopped, which may be the page finishing loading or content that changes more slowly than we watched. A person should watch the page for a minute to see whether anything keeps changing.

Criteria.TestCondition: All functionality can be accessed and executed using only the keyboard.
Criteria.TesterComment: We could not finish this test, so a person needs to check it. "Home" (link) works with a mouse but can't be reached with the keyboard; please check whether something else on the page does the same thing. "html > body > app-root > lib-search-story > div > app-hea..." can't be reached with the keyboard, but "NASA Logo" (link) does the same thing (The div in the header goes to the SDE home page. It is likely the Science Discovery Engine logo. The reached NASA link goes to nasa.gov, not the SDE home, so it is not the same. Button 2 'SDE' is unclear. Not certain.). If you disagree, tell your assistant. We looked for: things a mouse can click that the keyboard never reaches, including inside frames; menus that open when the mouse rests on them; custom controls that ignore Enter and Space; and tooltips with information found nowhere else. Results are for the browser used (version 153.0.8010.12).

Criteria.TestCondition: Individual keystrokes do not require specific timings for activation of functionality.
DisabilityImpact: With Limited Language, Cognitive, and Learning Abilities
Criteria.TesterComment: The page mentions holding or timing (The sentences are about rain flowing rapidly and erosion. They say nothing about keys or key timing.), but not for using the keyboard.

Criteria.TestCondition: There is no keyboard trap.
Criteria.TesterComment: We moved through the whole page with Tab and with Shift+Tab, and keyboard focus never got trapped. The page seems to load more content as you scroll, and the recording could not show all of it; content after the feed was reached only by Shift+Tab from the end.

Criteria.TestCondition: A visible indication of focus is provided when focus is on the interface component.
DisabilityImpact: With Limited Language, Cognitive, and Learning Abilities
Criteria.TesterComment: Some elements don't show when they have keyboard focus, so keyboard users can lose track of where they are. When "SDE SDE" (button) gets focus, nothing on or around it changes that we could see, so keyboard users can't tell focus is there. To see it, load the page and press Tab 2 times. If you can see a focus indicator we missed, tell your assistant. We could not get a clear before-and-after view of "Help and Support" (button) (scrolled out of view before the next step), so a person needs to check whether it shows focus: load the page and press Tab 3 times. 5 other element(s) showed focus clearly.

Criteria.TestCondition: When an interface component receives focus, it does not initiate an unexpected change of context.
DisabilityImpact: With Limited Language, Cognitive, and Learning Abilities
Criteria.TesterComment: Moving keyboard focus onto some elements changes what the user is doing without their asking, which can disorient keyboard and screen reader users. When "NASA Logo" (link) gets keyboard focus, the page goes to another address without the user choosing to. To see it, load the page and press Tab. When "next-icon" (button) gets keyboard focus, the page goes to another address without the user choosing to. To see it, load the page and press Shift+Tab.
Criteria.location: e1 [M4 FAIL] navigation after Tab: "NASA Logo" (link)

Criteria.TestCondition: The focus order preserves the meaning and operability of the web page.
DisabilityImpact: With Limited Language, Cognitive, and Learning Abilities
Criteria.TesterComment: Keyboard focus moves through the page in an order that follows how it reads, forward and backward. The focus order departs from the reading order (focus jumps back up the page from "Help and Support" (button) to "image slide My Search Stories Submit Your Story..."), but it still makes sense: Focus goes through the header (logo, SDE, help), then the main slide and its buttons (Submit, Search, next) in reading order. The jump back up is just the slide container starting at the page top.. If you disagree, tell your assistant.
